intended_object: A nilpotent Lie module: a module M over a Lie algebra L whose lower central series M ⊇ [L,M] ⊇ [L,[L,M]] ⊇ … reaches 0 after finitely many steps. This comes from the docstring.
explanation: The class asks for some k with `lowerCentralSeries ℤ L M k = ⊥`, which is the standard definition of a nilpotent Lie module. Using ℤ as the scalar ring is a design choice that makes the class independent of the base ring R. When `LieModule R L M` holds, the R-span of the brackets ⁅x, m⁆ is the same as their ℤ-span, because r•⁅x,m⁆ = ⁅x, r•m⁆. So the series over ℤ and over R have the same underlying sets. The next lemma in the file, `isNilpotent_iff`, proves this equivalence via `coe_lowerCentralSeries_eq_int`. The definition only needs a Lie ring acting on an additive group, so it is stated in full generality. Degenerate cases also come out right: the zero module is nilpotent with k = 0. When M = L with the adjoint action, it gives the usual nilpotent Lie algebra.
